tldr: This paper presents the first systematic survey of self-evolving agents, organizing the field around three foundational dimensions—what to evolve, when to evolve, and how to evolve—and positioning self-evolving agents as a pathway toward Artificial Super Intelligence.
contributions: Provides the first systematic and comprehensive review of self-evolving agents
Organizes the field around three foundational dimensions: what to evolve, when to evolve, and how to evolve
Introduces a formal definition of self-evolving agents based on a POMDP framework
Clarifies the relationship between self-evolving agents and other learning paradigms (curriculum learning, lifelong learning, model editing, unlearning)
Analyzes evaluation metrics, benchmarks, and applications in domains such as coding, education, and healthcare
Identifies critical challenges and research directions in safety, scalability, and co-evolutionary dynamics
methods: The authors define self-evolving agents formally within a POMDP framework where an agent system consists of LLMs, context (prompts and memory), and tools. They introduce a self-evolving strategy that recurrently transforms an agent system based on trajectories and feedback signals to maximize cumulative utility. The survey organizes evolution along four pillars—models, context, tools, and architecture—and classifies methods by evolutionary stage (intra-test-time vs. inter-test-time) and feedback type (scalar rewards, textual feedback, single-agent vs. multi-agent systems).
results: The survey identifies key methods including SCA, Self-Rewarding Self-Improving, SELF, SCoRe, PAG, TextGrad, and AutoRule for model evolution; Reflexion, AdaPlanner, Self-Refine, and RAGEN for lesson/context evolution; EvoMac, AgentCoder, and QuantAgent for tool evolution; and multi-agent frameworks like MAS-Zero and ReMA for architectural evolution. The paper highlights that fully autonomous self-evolution remains an aspirational goal, with current methods ranging from proto-evolution (iterative bootstrapping, feedback-driven prompting) to strong self-evolution (fully autonomous diagnosis and reconfiguration).
limitations: Fully autonomous self-evolution without human intervention remains an aspirational goal rather than the current norm. The field lacks established evaluation metrics and benchmarks tailored specifically for self-evolving agents. Critical challenges remain in safety, scalability, and co-evolutionary dynamics. The rapidly forming field makes it difficult to impose rigid exclusion thresholds, potentially including early-stage developments alongside more mature approaches.
